headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while pdf.js can ingest browser-rendered PDFs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and runs browsers, while Roo Code can use browsers, MCP, and shared workspace files. A malicious PDF or rendered content could be copied into Roo Code’s workspace or browser context and treated as instructions. The shared filesystem and browser surfaces make the pathway plausible in default use.
conditions: IF a PDF opened by pdf.js contains attacker-controlled instruction-like text AND Roo Code reads the rendered output or copied file into its workspace
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory or browser session
mitigations: Keep pdf.js and Roo Code in separate directories
Disable MCP servers in Roo Code for this workflow
Review PDFs in a read-only viewer before passing outputs onward
Use a manual human step before any Roo Code action on PDF-derived text

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF documents, and Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write plus network egress. If both touch the same workspace, PDF contents can flow from pdf.js into Roo Code and then out to external APIs or MCP servers. That creates a realistic leakage path for sensitive document data in default configurations.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are opened in pdf.js inside a workspace that Roo Code can read
IF Roo Code sends workspace context to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside Roo Code’s workspace
Turn off networked model calls for the session
Use a separate local-only workspace for PDF review
Redact documents before handing them to Roo Code
Clear workspace artifacts after processing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances via shared workspace files. pdf.js also handles files and can run browser-based tests. If both operate on the same workspace, concurrent edits or git changes can collide without locking, risking lost work or corrupted state. The overlap is broad enough to be dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same VS Code workspace or git checkout
IF Roo Code performs writes while pdf.js-generated artifacts are still being produced or updated
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git operations while pdf.js is generating artifacts
Use branch-per-agent isolation
Add a manual file-locking convention

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted or rendered document content, and Roo Code can act on workspace files and browser screenshots. If Roo Code treats pdf.js output as authoritative without verification, errors or malicious content can cascade into code changes, package installs, or other actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses pdf.js output as the sole source for code or task decisions
IF no human or automated verification step checks the extracted text
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before actions
Compare extracted text against the original PDF
Disable auto-execution of shell/package actions
Use checksum or page-reference checks on PDF-derived facts

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents, while Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys with broad network egress. If regulated PDFs or embedded personal data are processed in the shared workspace, Roo Code may transmit that data to third-party APIs, creating a retention/residency mismatch risk. The profiles do not show a dedicated compliance boundary.
conditions: IF PDFs contain regulated personal data or confidential records
IF Roo Code is configured to send context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Use non-regulated sample PDFs only
Disable cloud model calls for regulated data
Separate regulated-document handling from coding workspaces
Review retention settings before processing
Purge logs and workspace artifacts after use
